# 2024 Wyoming Primary fixtures, multi-county reference set

Real, official 2024 Wyoming Primary results across five counties spanning
the size range this feature has to handle: **Big Horn** (small, 13
precincts), **Fremont** (medium, 32 precincts), **Natrona** (medium-large,
46 precincts), **Campbell** (large, 37 precincts), **Laramie** (largest by
population, 40 precincts, 17 concurrent contests). Pulled from the Secretary
of State's official 2024 archive to design and validate the 2026
election-results schema/adapters *before* any 2026 source data exists.

**This is all 2024 data. None of it may ever be served, labeled, or
confused with 2026 results**, it exists purely as realistic input for
scaffolding and adapter testing.

## Source

All five counties come from the same official package:

- Landing page: https://sos.wyo.gov/Elections/Docs/2024/2024PrimaryResults.aspx
- ZIP archive: https://sos.wyo.gov/Elections/Docs/2024/Results/Primary/2024_Wyoming_Primary_Results.zip
  (not checked in, 677KB, all 23 counties across 3 workbooks; re-download
  directly if more counties are needed)
- County-specific PDFs: `https://sos.wyo.gov/Elections/Docs/2024/Results/Primary/2024_{County}_County_Primary_PbP.pdf`

Each `2024-<county>/` folder has its own `raw/` (untouched source data) and
`normalized/` (output of the shared reference parser). See each folder for
its specific file inventory, the shape is identical across all five.

## Per-county comparison

| County | Precincts | Contests | Precinct rows (normalized) | Reconciliation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Big Horn | 13 | 6 (US Senate/House, SD20, HD26–28) | 423 | 0 mismatches |
| Fremont | 32 | 9 (US Senate/House, SD20/26, HD28/33/34/54/55) | 1,088 | 0 mismatches |
| Natrona | 46 | 14 (US Senate/House, SD2/28/30, HD35–38/56–59/62) | 1,530 | 0 mismatches |
| Campbell | 37 | 8 (US Senate/House, SD24, HD3/31/32/52/53) | 1,065 | 0 mismatches |
| Laramie | 40 | 17 (US Senate/House, SD4/6/8, HD4/7–12/41–44/61) | 1,285 | 0 mismatches |

"Reconciliation" = every precinct-level candidate/write-in/overvote/undervote
row, summed per contest, compared against that county sheet's own official
`Total` row. **All five counties reconcile exactly, with zero mismatches,
after the fixes below were applied**, this was not true on the first pass.

## Findings that changed the schema/parser design

These came from hitting real inconsistencies across counties, not from
reading the format spec, several only appeared once a *second* or *third*
county was checked against the first:

1. **`-` means "structurally not applicable," not zero.** A precinct not in
   a given legislative district shows `-` for every candidate in that
   contest. Must be *omitted* as a row, never zero-filled, otherwise
   precinct participation math and any "precincts reporting" count are
   wrong for every multi-district county (i.e. all of them; every county
   here splits across 2+ legislative districts except none did, all five
   split across multiple House/Senate districts).

2. **Column A can contain non-precinct junk, and it's not rare.** `"Precincts
   Continue\non Next Page"`, page-break footer text, leaked into the
   precinct column on **3 of 5 counties (Natrona, Laramie, Campbell)**,
   silently inflating precinct counts by exactly one until filtered
   explicitly by content (`"continue"` / `"page"` substring match), not by
   position or row count. It appears **only on the larger/busier sheets**
   (16, 17, 14 contest-columns respectively), consistent with a
   spreadsheet-to-print pagination artifact that shows up once a sheet is
   tall enough to need an internal print break. **This was caught only
   because a second and third county were checked against Natrona; Natrona's
   own fixture initially shipped with a silently-wrong `precincts_total`
   of 47 instead of 46 until Laramie/Campbell exposed the same defect and
   forced a proper fix.** This is the single strongest argument in this
   whole exercise for validating any parser against *multiple* real
   sources before trusting it, not just one clean-looking example.

10. **A fixed row-count guess for "where does the source end" is fragile
    the same way a fixed contest list is.** The `raw/*_sheet_verbatim.csv`
    dumps were originally generated by pre-computing an expected row range
    (`5 header rows + precincts_total + 1`) rather than locating the
    sheet's own `Total` row by value. That worked for 3 of 5 counties by
    coincidence and silently truncated Laramie's and Campbell's raw dumps
    *before* their `Total` row, invisible until the production parser
    (`extract_election_results_xlsx.py`, which correctly refuses to run
    without a `Total` row rather than emit unverified data) hard-failed on
    them. Fixed by locating `row[0] == 'Total'` directly rather than
    counting rows. Same lesson as finding #2, applied one layer up: never
    trust a derived row count where a direct value match is available.

3. **The "Total Ballots Cast" companion workbook has its own `Total` row
   too**, in the same column-A position as a real precinct label, on every
   county checked. A naive `if row[0]` filter silently included it as
   precinct #14/#33/#41/#38, inflating ballots-cast row counts by exactly
   one across the board until filtered by an explicit `!= "Total"` check
   (same category of bug as #2, see the pattern: **never trust a filter
   that isn't matching by explicit value**).

4. **The two companion workbooks (precinct results vs. ballots cast) do not
   automatically agree on precinct count** even after both known artifacts
   are filtered, this project confirmed they *do* match exactly (Big Horn
   13/13, Fremont 32/32, Natrona 46/46, Campbell 37/37, Laramie 40/40) once
   both bugs above were fixed, but that agreement should be treated as a
   **runtime validation check for the production parser**, not an assumption
   baked into the code. Two companion files from the same official source
   silently disagreeing is exactly the kind of "structural change" the
   original results-feature spec asked to flag for review rather than
   trust blindly.

5. **Write-ins/overvotes/undervotes are contest-level ballot categories,
   never candidates.** Confirmed present and structurally identical across
   all five counties, they need a `row_type` discriminator so no adapter
   ever alias-matches "Write-Ins" against `candidates.slug`.

6. **Contest lists are genuinely per-county, not a fixed statewide set.**
   Each county's sheet only contains the WY Senate/House districts that
   physically overlap it (Big Horn: 4 legislative districts; Laramie: 12).
   A parser must read whatever contest columns a given sheet actually has, never assume a fixed contest count or hardcode a district list.

7. **This SOS package is federal + WY Senate/House only, confirmed across
   all five counties.** Zero county-commissioner or municipal contest data
   anywhere in it, at any county size. The two-track architecture (SOS
   archive for federal/legislative vs. each county clerk's own site for
   county/local races) is now evidence-backed across a size range, not just
   a single county.

8. **One SOS-generated format serves all 23 counties for this track**, important scoping correction to the original "build 23 different
   parsers" framing. Because the *official SOS archive* is centrally
   generated (one Excel export tool, 23 sheets, one page-layout engine),
   **a single `xlsx_wide_header` adapter is very plausibly sufficient for
   all 23 counties' federal/legislative results**, once it correctly
   handles findings #1–4 above. The "one adapter per county" burden from
   the original spec applies much more to the **election-night unofficial
   track**, each county clerk's own independently hosted page, which
   this fixture set deliberately does not cover yet (it's all *official*,
   post-canvass data). That's the next thing worth sampling for real, since
   it's a genuinely different problem than what these fixtures solve.

9. **PDF text extraction loses the candidate-name line break**
   (`"John\nBarrasso"` in XLSX → `"JohnBarrasso"` via `pypdf` on the PDF),
   confirmed on Natrona's PDF specifically; not re-verified on the other
   four PDFs in this pass (they were downloaded and checksummed for
   provenance/future use but not text-extracted). XLSX/CSV should be the
   adapter's preferred source whenever a county offers both; PDF stays a
   last-resort/manual-verification format.

## What's genuinely still untested

- **No county-clerk-hosted (non-SOS) format has been sampled yet.** Every
  finding above is about the *one* SOS-generated format. The
  election-night "unofficial results" track, each of the 23 county clerk
  websites, could look completely different from this, and from each
  other. That's the next real unknown, not a variation on what's here.
- **No partial/in-progress reporting state exists in any of this data**, it's all fully certified/canvassed, so every county shows
  `precincts_reporting == precincts_total`. The "partial results," "county
  reporting complete" vs. "stale source," and embargo-state UI work still
  needs hand-built or synthesized fixtures for those states; real 2024 data
  can't provide them.
- County-commissioner/municipal/precinct-committee contest data, outside
  this SOS package entirely (finding #7), remains completely unsampled.
